articles.title: Key federal panel approves Trump’s arch while it is being challenged in court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A federal judge late on Thursday (November 5, 2026) blocked the Trump administration from breaking ground on a towering memorial arch for 14 days.

The temporary restraining order by U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, halting the work, represents a major setback for one of President Donald Trump’s most prominent projects in his vision to remake Washington.

The decision followed a series of steps taken earlier on Thursday by the government, including the final approval of the arch by the National Capital Planning Commission in an 8-4 vote after a hearing of nine and a half hours, where dozens of witnesses opposed the construction.

The administration said the work could begin as soon as the approval was in place, the Interior Department issued a final decision authorising construction and the National Park Service published the proper notification.
In issuing the temporary stop, Judge Chutkan said Virginia and the District of Columbia had shown that the immediacy of the construction would cause real harm to the plaintiffs.

“The harm is certain,” she wrote. “Defendants initially notified the court that construction could begin as early as November 5, 2026, if the NCPC approves the project at its meeting that day and the Department of the Interior authorizes construction.” In their filing, Virginia and the District of Columbia warned of traffic pattern distortions, as well as concerns about the impact on mutual aid emergency calls if the arch were to proceed.

“Second, the District and Virginia will incur significant unrecoverable costs. As soon as construction begins, DDOT [District Department of Transportation] will need to expend staff time and operating resources to affirmatively and proactively manage temporary detours, crashes or disabled vehicles,” Judge Chutkan wrote.

The judge’s decision came just over an hour after the commission’s hearing ended. The final vote came after nine and a half hours and scores of people opposing it. The vote broke along federal and local lines. Those in favour work for the administration or are connected to the President, who was pushing for the immediate construction. Opponents represented the city of Washington.

The remote, call-in hearing — which crashed repeatedly in the first few hours and was accompanied by a nearly universally negative comment section — drew witnesses who gave impassioned comments opposing an arch they said will destroy the solemnity of the nearby Arlington National Cemetery, where hundreds of thousands of fallen service members and military veterans are buried.
The panel’s Trump-appointed chairman launched the meeting with a gushing appraisal of the towering monument and lauded Mr. Trump for wanting to build it.

“President Trump understands as president and a superb builder that it’s important to our national identity to display who we are through grand monuments,” said Mark Paoletta, the commission’s chairman.

As Mr. Trump has often remarked, “the great cities around the world have arches: Paris, Rome, London,” said Mr. Paoletta, who also serves as general counsel for the White House Office of Management and Budget.

articles.title: US midterm election results 2026: Key Indian-origin winners
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Many Indian-origin candidates too notched up victories as Democrats captured majorities in both the Senate and House, sweeping victories that reached deep into Republican strongholds as tens of millions of voters delivered a scathing rebuke to ​President Donald Trump.

Indian-American candidates Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives from Virginia and Florida, respectively. India-born Nithya Raman too has won the Los Angeles mayoral race. On the other hand, Republican ‌Vivek ‌Ramaswamy ‌was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor.

Kerala-born Nithya Raman has won the Los Angeles mayoral race, becoming the first Indian-American elected to lead the city, as incumbent Karen Bass conceded defeat and pledged a smooth transition. The most recent Los Angeles County electoral updates, refreshed at 4:34 pm local time, recorded Raman holding 460,772 ballots, equivalent to 52.70 per cent, compared with Bass’s 413,519 votes, representing 47.30 per cent.

Her lead expanded to 47,253 votes, marking a significant increase from the 34,654-vote advantage reported during the morning count, though these figures remain provisional while electoral staff continue processing votes cast on Tuesday.

Suhas Subramanyam, who served as an advisor to former president Barack Obama, has been re-elected as a member of the US House of Representatives. The 40-year-old won from Virginia’s 10th congressional district , polling over 61.5% of the vote against Republican Dave Beckwith, who managed to win 36.4 per cent of the ballots cast.

Ro Khanna has won re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, located in the heart of Silicon Valley. The 50-year-old is completing his fifth term and will begin his sixth in January. Khanna was born in Philadelphia to a middle-class family. Both his parents immigrated to the United States from India in the 1970s.

Pramila Jayapal, who represents Washington’s 7th Congressional District, has secured a sixth term in the House of Representatives. Last month, her criticism of India’s Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls drew a public rebuke from India’s ambassador to the US. Jayapal, who was first elected to Congress in 2016, has been a prominent voice on immigration reform and healthcare issues.

A former high school principal, Pia Dandiya became the newest Indian-American to be elected to the US House , defeating Republican Casey Askar in Florida’s 22nd Congressional district. Dandiya bagged 51.9% of the votes, while her opponent Askar polled 49.1% of the votes.

Indian-American Democratic lawmaker Ami Bera has won the re-election to the U.S. House in California’s 3rd Congressional District, defeating Republican Robb Tucker. The 61-year-old won his eighth term in the US House of Representatives. Physician-turned-politician Amerish Babulal ‘Ami’ Bera is the longest-serving Indian American in the US Congress and is considered a strong voice on healthcare and diplomacy, as per PTI.
Amish Shah , an Indian-American physician, has been elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in Arizona’s First Congressional District.
He has now become the sixth Indian American to be elected to the U.S. House of Representatives.
Shah, a three-term member of Arizona House of Representatives, defeated Republican Jay Feely, a former National Football League(NFL) player, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump.

articles.title: Mahabharata, Arthashastra, Rajatarangini manuscripts added to UNESCO memory regional register
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Manuscripts of the epic Mahabharata, Kalhana’s 12th-century historical chronicle Rajatarangini, and Kautilya’s Arthashastra, a work on governance and statecraft, have been inscribed on UNESCO’s Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, officials said on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
PIB Culture made the announcement on X and shared photos of UNESCO certificates.

“A moment of immense pride for India! The Rajatarangini, Mahabharata and Arthashastra have been inscribed in @UNESCO’s Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, marking a historic milestone in the global recognition of India’s rich civilisational heritage!” it said.

🇮🇳 A moment of immense pride for India! The Rājataraṅgiṇī, Mahābhārata and Arthaśāstra have been inscribed in @UNESCO's Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, marking a historic milestone in the global recognition of India's rich civilisational heritage! https://t.co/LjJwIILhmf
The decision was taken at the 11th Session of the Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register held in Jakarta, Indonesia, the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) said.
According to an official, the IGNCA played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.
Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat hailed the inscriptions as a landmark recognition of India’s extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage.

“A moment of immense pride for India! The inclusion of Rajatarangini, Mahabharata and Arthashastra in @UNESCO Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register is a landmark recognition of India’s extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage,” he posted.

“These timeless works embody our rich traditions of historical inquiry, philosophical thought and statecraft, whose wisdom continues to inspire humanity. Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble PM Shri @narendramodi Ji, India’s civilisational legacy is receiving unprecedented global recognition and its rightful place on the world stage,” the minister added.

With the recognition, India’s historical, literary, philosophical and political thought receives wider international acknowledgement, taking the country’s total number of inscriptions in the Regional Register to six, officials said.

Illustrated manuscripts of the Ramcharitamanas, featuring intricate miniature paintings, preserving Tulsidas’ work; a rare 15th-century manuscript containing animal fables and moral stories from the Panchatantra; and the manuscript of the Sahrdayaloka-Locana, a text of Indian poetics, were inscribed in the regional register in 2024.

fullParagraphs: President Donald Trump will participate in a Deepavali celebration at the White House on Friday.
The celebrations are scheduled to be held at the Oval Office, continuing a tradition started by President George W Bush.
Earlier, the ceremonies were mostly held in the Eisenhower Executive Office Building in the presence of Indian-American community members and Indian diplomats.
In 2009, President Barack Obama became the first president to light a lamp (diya) at the White House, during a ceremony in the East Room.
Since then, lamp lighting ceremonies have been held in various locations in the White House, including the Oval Office and the Roosevelt Room.
Last year, India’s Ambassador to the U.S. Vinay Kwatra joined Mr. Trump in the Oval Office to celebrate Deepavali with the traditional lighting of the lamp.

articles.title: Indian NGO REACH receives Kochon Prize 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Resource group for Education and Advocacy for Community Health (REACH), a not-for-profit organisation working to strengthen the tuberculosis (TB) response in India, has been awarded the Kochon Prize 2026, becoming the first civil society, non-profit organisation from India to receive this prestigious global recognition for its contributions to combating TB, a press release said.

Presented by the Kochon Foundation, an independent Korean non-profit foundation, in partnership with the Stop TB Partnership, the Kochon Prize recognises individuals and organisations that have made significant contributions to the fight against TB. The 2026 Kochon Prize is shared by REACH, the Centre for Health Solutions, Kenya, and the Marshall Islands TB Control Program. Previous winners from India include L.S. Chauhan (2006), head of the Revised National TB Control Programme, the Indian Council of Medical Research (2017) and Molbio Diagnostics (2024). The award was presented at the Stop TB Partnership Board Meeting held in Indonesia on November 5, 2026.

“Treat the person, not the disease - our journey with TB communities has been just that. We realised early on that overcoming barriers to care means addressing more than clinical needs - it means recognising social, community, family, mental health and situational challenges. That is the essence of integrated care: seeing the whole person, understanding their realities, and doing whatever it takes to ensure that no one is left behind,” said Nalini Krishnan, chairperson and co-founder, REACH.

“REACH is a remarkable and rare organisation that has been consistently ahead of the curve in terms of public health action, and particularly in the field of TB. A women-led organisation, they genuinely care about the people they’re supporting, beyond the numbers, data and reports to donor. However, they combine this with a robust scientific and technical approach and a shrewd understanding of the public health landscape in the country,” said Soumya Swaminathan, chairperson, M. S. Swaminathan Research Foundation and former chief scientist, WHO, who nominated REACH for the award.

“This recognition is testimony to the dedication of the community health workers, TB Nanbans and TB Champions who work alongside us, and to the families affected by TB and non-communicable diseases (NCDs) who have placed their trust in us. We are deeply grateful to their unwavering commitment and fortitude, and are energised to do more to help facilitate equitable access to health,” said Ramya Ananthakrishnan, director, REACH.

articles.title: Documentary highlights role of family physicians in strengthening primary healthcare
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The role of family physicians in ensuring accessible, affordable and patient-centred healthcare came into focus at the premiere of the documentary ‘The Doctor Next Door: A Legacy of Care’, screened at the Indian Heritage Academy in Bengaluru earlier this week.

Through accounts of veteran physicians, patients and young medical professionals, the film examines the decline of neighbourhood family practices and the growing fragmentation of healthcare. It highlights how long-standing doctor-patient relationships built on trust, familiarity and personal attention remain central to effective primary care.

The documentary draws attention to the rising dependence on specialised and corporate hospital-based treatment, making a case for strengthening family medicine as the foundation of India’s healthcare system.

Swetha Reddy, project manager of the documentary, said the film features perspectives from young medical students and practitioners considering careers in general practice, highlighting the need for changes in medical education and healthcare policy to encourage family medicine.

Directed by Ganesh Shankar Raj of Mindia Films and produced in collaboration with the Academy of Family Physicians of India (AFPI), the non-profit documentary explores the enduring relationship between family doctors and patients, and the importance of continuity of care in an increasingly specialised healthcare system.

The screening was followed by a panel discussion featuring scientists, medical professionals, senior family physicians, and community health advocates. The discussion centred on the challenges facing primary healthcare, the need to strengthen family medicine, and the importance of human relationships in medical practice.
Veteran family physician B.C. Rao was among the contributors to the initiative, alongside representatives of AFPI and other healthcare professionals.

The organisers said the documentary was intended to initiate wider conversations on reviving primary healthcare networks in urban and rural communities, and recognising neighbourhood doctors as an integral part of the healthcare system.

articles.title: Amid the sparkle of Deepavali, ophthalmologists sound a note of caution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The sound of firecrackers filling the air is not far away as Deepavali draws closer. But the excitement of bursting firecrackers comes with a word of caution from ophthalmologists as they warn that a moment of carelessness can cause eye injuries ranging from minor abrasions to severe ocular trauma.

M. Elangovan, director, Regional Institute of Ophthalmology and Government Ophthalmic Hospital (RIO-GOH), Chennai, said that there are different types of crackers. “Bursting types (explosive crackers) will produce irregular, small and forcible particles in all directions and are the most dangerous. These particles can travel at such a velocity that they could hit or penetrate any soft surface. Then, there is direct heat injury caused by crackers such as sparklers that can cause scar formations in the cornea or conjunctiva due to the heat generated. Sudden and close exposure to bright light-emitting crackers can also cause bleaching or temporary blackout due to the impact on the rod and cone cells in the retina,” he explained.

articles.title: Cancer care: Long battle for affordable treatment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: A 45-year-old garment factory worker from Bengaluru Rural diagnosed with stage IV-A cancer of the mouth faces an arduous course of treatment: chemotherapy to shrink the tumour, extensive surgery involving reconstruction, followed by radiation and chemotherapy. The cost of medicines and supportive drugs of around ₹93,000 alone, besides treatment costs, are staggering for her family with a modest monthly income of ₹28,000. With funds running out, she is facing the risk of discontinuing the final stages of treatment.

Likewise, a 56-year-old shopkeeper from Mysuru district, diagnosed with recurrent, inoperable hypopharyngeal cancer involving the oesophagus, has a different but equally difficult challenge. After three cycles of chemotherapy, the disease has shown partial response. Immunotherapy could offer another treatment option, but its cost remains prohibitive. Spending another ₹2.4 lakh to ₹8 lakh over the next 2 to 3 months for bi-weekly immunotherapy is virtually impossible on a ₹45,000/month income.

articles.title: Deepavali with pets: Why pet parents are choosing quieter holiday getaways
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: As Deepavali approaches, pets often become anxious at the sound of firecrackers. Dogs and cats may hide under beds or in dark corners, while some lose interest in playtime, walks and even pee breaks. For pet owners, finding ways to ease their distress is an ongoing challenge. Some who love celebrating Deepavali but cannot bear to see their pets shivering and panting are now choosing quieter destinations to spend the festival.
Frodo from Bengaluru | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Pet parent JP Daisy boards her cat at a hostel in Hyderabad’s Kokapet with soundproof rooms during Deepavali. Watching her usually docile Siamese, Sharpay, run helter-skelter as firecracker noise peaks in the evening makes Daisy anxious. “She is a lightweight cat and usually eats very little. During Deepavali, she stops eating. One of our friends suggested a place to board her. Sharpay is not clingy, so boarding her is easy,” she says.

Pet boarding facilities also see a surge in demand during festivals, and not just from people travelling. With diyas lit in homes, unattended flames can pose a safety risk. At Pet Cafe Hyderabad, a boarding facility and restaurant in Banjara Hills, founder Deven Baheti says regulars book slots weeks, sometimes months, ahead of Deepavali.

“The open space and location make it comfortable for pets. Ours is a quiet locality, with few homes bursting firecrackers. To further drown out the noise, we play calming music, use vet-approved anti-anxiety drops and essential oils, and apply calming sprays to help them relax,” says Deven.

With boarding (charges of ₹1000 per day) slots fully booked, Deven and his team are preparing to keep the pets occupied with play and grooming sessions. “We do it for the love of animals. Even reactive pets are managed by a few of us and kept in separate enclosures, away from the friendly ones.”

Voicing use of vet-approved calming drops Bengaluru based Neeta Sharma said “That is the only way to calm our pet rescued Indie Frodo. The other two a labrador and a Beagle don’t care much about the sound.”
A boarder at Pet Cafe Hyd | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Not all pet parents can board their pets, or are comfortable with the idea. Many instead look for pet-friendly homestays and resorts away from the city. With several properties now welcoming pets, finding the right one is the only challenge. In Chevella, about 50 kilometres from Hyderabad, homestays have become a welcome respite for pet owners. Ramya R, a pet parent, says the search for a suitable getaway begins soon after Ganesh Chaturthi. “The crackers on visarjan days are a reminder that we need to start looking.”

Pollam Gattu, a farmhouse in Chevella surrounded by carrot and flower fields, has become their regular Deepavali escape. The area sees fewer firecrackers than the city, making it a quieter retreat. “In villages, it is relatively quieter than in the city. I can’t say it is absolutely silent, but it is not as noisy with firecrackers as the city is,” she says.

What about Deepavali puja and other rituals? “We keep the decor light at home. One of our cousins stays back for a few hours to keep the doors open. It is all a matter of arrangement and coordination. In the end, our two-year-old Labrador comes home happy.”

At K-Resorts in Puducherry, almost all of its 56 villas are occupied by pet owners seeking respite from Deepavali noise. Founder Prateek Shah says, “This is the time of year when demand comes not from the holiday crowd but from families in Tamil Nadu looking for a quieter place to celebrate Deepavali.”

articles.title: Google sued over suicide-related AI chats on school computer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer.

Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant's low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world.

The teenager was not able to access Google's Gemini app, nor OpenAI's ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google's search engine, which contains AI-powered tools.
Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students.

"Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they're interacting with AI," Andrew Liddell, one of the family's attorneys, told AFP on Thursday.
The complaint alleges that the child had been a "happy 13-year-old girl" in North Carolina who received great grades, played music and participated in Girl Scouts.

Despite "no history" of mental illness, within months of using Google's AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a "quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis" according to the complaint.
On March 17, the school's monitoring software flagged a document titled "Funeral," and the school notified her parents.
Her mother then saw the child writing a farewell letter in real-time after logging into her daughter's account, and her father intervened.
"We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously," Google spokesperson Jose Castaneda told AFP.
Google argues that AI mode includes safeguards against self-harm and attempts to bypass them.
But the child "was able to keep going back over and over and over again," Liddle said. "Whatever safeguards they think they put in place were obviously insufficient."

articles.title: Trump debacle: On the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan , making him the first Muslim Senator in history ; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate ; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.title: Helping hand: On Cyclones Arnab and Murasu
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Long-term preparedness and a swift response by authorities minimised casualties when the back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu hit two places of the Andhra Pradesh coast. In Andhra Pradesh, damage from Cyclone Arnab , which made landfall on October 28 was estimated at roughly ₹4,526 crore. Initial estimates of the damage by Cyclone Murasu, which crossed the coast on November 3, indicate that about 52,500 hectares of standing crops were affected. The State reported 12 deaths from the two cyclones. The first cyclone damaged nearly 90,000 hectares of standing crops in southern parts of Odisha. After preliminary on-the-spot assessment of flood-hit areas, the Union government is expected to soon release the first instalment of funds to the affected States. Personnel from Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu have also gone to the rescue of Andhra Pradesh.

The deployment of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) and other technologies has significantly reduced human casualties and property damage. During Cyclone Hudhud in October 2014, Andhra Pradesh reported 63 deaths and damage estimated at nearly ₹22,000 crore. As natural disasters become more frequent in India, greater collaboration is needed between higher learning institutions, especially in science and technology, and central and State government agencies. Authorities must develop an effective compensation framework for saving crops/crop losses. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, a crop insurance scheme that was launched by the Union government a decade ago, has not provided farmers with comprehensive safety cover, as they suffer due to the vagaries of nature. The Union government should improve the scheme so that all farmers are encouraged to bring their crops under the scheme, while State governments should raise awareness about the insurance scheme and support agriculturists by topping up benefits that are under the insurance cover. The Centre should also focus on financial assistance for permanent restoration projects. The initial stand of the Union government was that the National and State Disaster Response Funds were meant for response and relief, not recovery and reconstruction, but following the 15th Finance Commission’s nudge, it added recovery and reconstruction as a component of the two funds two years ago. However, when public infrastructure suffers extensive damage, the Centre should provide additional assistance to ease the burden on affected States. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his team at the Centre must act in the spirit of “cooperative federalism”.

articles.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself . Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack.

So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. If the fear is that cryptocurrencies are not backed by any asset, then Indian policymakers can choose to allow only stablecoins, which do have real assets underpinning them. Indians are not at higher risk from cryptos than they are from fake stock market scams. The best defence is awareness. By refusing to regulate the crypto space in India and, indeed, taxing it at a prohibitive rate, the government is driving Indians towards either the black market, where such scams proliferate, or foreign exchanges. The government can take a leaf out of Binance’s book and mandate an industry-maintained emergency fund. There is ample international legislation to emulate now. The point is, crypto risks have fallen and adoption is rising. Now is the time to regulate the industry.

articles.title: MPTC/ZPTC elections: clashes erupt between YSRCP, TDP activists in Kadapa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Clashes broke out between the YSRCP and the TDP activists at several areas of Kadapa district on Thursday morning (November 5, 2026) during the MPTC and ZPTC elections.

According to sources, a quarrel broke out between the agents of YSRCP and TDP near a polling station in Yerripalli village, Pulivendla mandal, of the district. The groups engaged in heated arguments, and allegedly some of them hurled petrol bombs. None were injured in the clash.

Speaking to The Hindu , Pulivendla Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Murali Nayak stated, “The activists of both parties used firecrackers, which were brought to celebrate after victory, to attack each other. They took out petrol from their bikes to escalate the fight. However, the police controlled them within five minutes.”

articles.title: Sabarimala gears up for pilgrimage season
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chalakayam-Pampa road will be ready for the Sabarimala pilgrimage season by November 12, with road markings to be completed by November 15.

The arrangements for the upcoming pilgrimage season, which begins on November 16, were reviewed at a meeting chaired by Revenue Minister A P Anilkumar at Pampa on Thursday. Round-the-clock integrated control rooms will function at Pampa, Nilackal and Sannidhanam, with nodal officers from key departments coordinating the arrangements. Crowd monitoring will cover 18 sectors at Sannidhanam and 15 sectors across Pampa and Nilackal.

Twenty-two emergency medical centres along the pilgrimage and forest routes will become operational by November 10. Three ambulances will be stationed at Sannidhanam, while an off-road ambulance will be deployed on the forest route for the first time. A 120-member volunteer team will provide stretcher services, and CPR facilities will be available at all 22 centres.

Under the ‘Nirmalam Sabarimala’ initiative, a major sanitation drive will be held along the district’s main roads leading to Sabarimala on November 9. The aim is to make these roads waste-free by November 15. Around 1,000 sanitation workers will be deployed at Pampa, Nilackal and Sannidhanam. The Clean Kerala Company has already removed nearly 50 tonnes of old waste and scrap.

The Motor Vehicles Department will implement the Safe Zone project on the Pampa-Laha stretch, with round-the-clock road safety patrols and mobile workshop facilities. An AI-based parking system will be introduced at Nilackal. KSRTC buses and tractors have undergone safety checks, and drivers have received training.

Drinking water and refreshments will be provided to pilgrims waiting in queues from the first day of the season. A prepaid counter will regulate dolly charges, while toilets at Pampa and Sannidhanam will be free. The KSEB will set up a fast-charging facility for electric vehicles at Pampa, capable of charging four vehicles simultaneously.

The Devaswom Board has increased production capacity and stocked raw materials to ensure an uninterrupted supply of appam and aravana. An emergency operations officer has been posted at Pampa to coordinate disaster response.

With nearly 80% of Sabarimala pilgrims passing through Chengannur, Health and Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan has directed departments to ensure food safety, safe drinking water and adequate medical facilities along the pilgrimage route. He also reviewed arrangements at Pandalam, another key pilgrim centre.

At a meeting held at the Kallissery rest house during the day, the Minister stressed the need for vigilance against communicable diseases in view of the influx of pilgrims from across the country. Food safety inspections at hotels and food distribution centres will be intensified. The KSEB and Kerala Water Authority were asked to ensure uninterrupted power and water supply.

The police will deploy 140 personnel, 100 special police officers and 25 home guards, besides operating a 24-hour control room. The KSRTC will operate 60 buses initially and increase the fleet to 80 during peak periods. A 24-hour clinic will function at Chengannur railway station, while six beds and four ICU beds have been reserved for pilgrims at the hospital.

At Pandalam, the Irrigation Department will maintain bathing ghats and install warning boards, while the Forest Department will clear the Thiruvabharanam route of dangerous trees and branches. The KSRTC will operate special services between Pandalam and Pampa. Medical facilities, medicines and ambulances will also be ensured along the route.

articles.title: TGSRTC bus swerves to avoid motorcycle, hits electric pole in Jagtial

fullParagraphs: A TGSRTC bus rammed into an electric pole while trying to avoid hitting a motorcycle at a U-turn on the Medipalli highway in Ibrahimpatnam mandal of Jagtial district on Thursday.

According to sources, the incident occurred when the driver of the bus, which was travelling from Nizamabad towards Metpalli, applied sudden brakes to avoid hitting the motorcycle. The bus veered off the road and rammed into a roadside electric pole.
The motorcycle rider, identified as Lakshman of Bandalingapur village in the same mandal, sustained injuries after reportedly falling off his two-wheeler.
He was shifted to a hospital in Jagtial for treatment. None of the bus passengers were injured in the incident. However, the front portion of the bus was damaged in the impact.

articles.title: School excursion row: UDF leaders release CCTV footage in support of their claims
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The controversy surrounding the recent student study tour conducted by the Meenangadi Government Higher Secondary School saw new developments on Thursday (November 5), with the United Democratic Front (UDF) Meenangadi panchayat committee releasing CCTV footage allegedly showing school Principal, Shivi Krishnan, and the Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) president Hijas Ulladan entering a bar.

At a press conference, UDF leaders, led by former Meenangadi panchayat president K.E. Vinayan, presented the footage purportedly retrieved from the bar in Nampally, Hyderabad. The leadership claimed that the visuals showed the principal and the PTA president entering and leaving the establishment, alleging that a bill of ₹1,100 for alcoholic beverages was settled using the PTA president’s personal ATM card.

Following the disclosure, the UDF Meenangadi leadership lodged a formal complaint with the Wayanad District Police Chief and announced plans to approach the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights. They alleged that students who spoke in support of the school authorities were subjected to severe cyberbullying, intimidation, and harsh online trials by vloggers and online media outlets.

The row originally erupted after allegations emerged that two responsible school officials had consumed alcohol during a recent study tour to Hyderabad. Responding to the accusations, Principal Shivi Krishnan, who is also a leader of a left-leaning teachers’ association, had refuted the claims and termed them a targeted political move against him.

Though a subsequent medical examination of the principal revealed no presence of alcohol in his blood and a section of students publicly defended him, the UDF countered that online media and vloggers were influenced to sway public opinion, prompting them to release the CCTV footage to substantiate their allegations.

articles.title: No application for renewal of helicopter service was pending before govt. when CM took special flight, Keralam SPC tells Lok Ayuktha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: State Police Chief (SPC) Ravada Chandrasekhar informed the Lok Ayuktha that no application from Chipson Aviation for extending helicopter service was pending before the State government when Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan undertook a special flight journey to oversee relief operations in rain-hit areas of Malappuram recently. He added that the Chief Minister had not gained any pecuniary benefit by undertaking the journey.

The agreement between the SPC and the company for wet leasing the helicopter service stood automatically terminated on September 19, 2026. As per Clause 16 of the agreement, it shall stand automatically terminated on expiry on September 19/09/2026 and any decision for its extension had to be taken before the expiry of the agreement. However, no decision was taken for its extension as the government did not intend to proceed further in the matter.

The Chief Minister, who also holds the portfolio of disaster management, decided to visit Nilambur, T.K. Colony, Pookkothumpadam, where six people were swept away on September 20 in a flash flood in the Kottapuzha river, Mr. Chandrasekhar informed a Division Bench consisting of Lok Ayuktha N. Anilkumar and Upa Lok Ayuktha Ashok Menon.

Mr. Chandrasekhar termed the allegation of the petitioner, K.M. Shajahan, that after the expiry of the existing agreement, Chipsan Aviation had submitted a proposal for providing helicopter services on a pay-per-use basis and a twin-engine helicopter was reportedly offered at ₹24 lakh per flying hour and a single-engine helicopter at ₹23.2 lakh per flying hour as false and baseless.

As the government had no intention to renew or invite a fresh bid for hiring a helicopter, the allegation that the firm had a direct and substantial commercial interest in a matter to be decided by the State government was absolutely false, he submitted.
The Lok Ayuktha later issued notice to the State Chief Secretary in the case..

fullParagraphs: Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy has said completion of the Srisailam Left Bank Canal (SLBC) tunnel project would enable Telangana to draw water from the dead storage level of the Srisailam reservoir and provide irrigation to farmers even during severe drought conditions.

Addressing the newly constituted Nalgonda Agricultural Market Committee governing body on Thursday, he said the SLBC project was conceived at an estimated cost of ₹2,000 crore to resolve the fluoride problem and provide irrigation facilities across Nalgonda district.

The project had remained stalled during the previous government’s tenure. The Congress government resumed the works after coming to power, but they were halted again due to the accident. The works had recently resumed and were progressing at a brisk pace, he said.

MLC Shankar Naik, Nalgonda Mayor Burri Chaitanya Srinivas Reddy, former municipal chairman Srinivas Reddy, former ZPTC member Gummala Mohan Reddy and Assistant Director of Marketing Department Chaya Devi were among those present.

B. Hemalatha Venkat Reddy took oath as chairman of the Nalgonda Agricultural Market Committee, while V. Srinivas Goud assumed charge as vice-chairman. The directors also took oath administered by Ms. Chaya Devi.

articles.title: CBG blending at 1.7% in H1; pipeline connectivity key to achieving 3% target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India achieved 1.7% blending of compressed biogas (CBG) with domestic piped natural gas (D-PNG) and vehicular compressed natural gas (CNG) in the first half of the current fiscal, but will need an acceleration in sales during the second half to meet the mandated 3% target, according to the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB).
The country has set a blending target of 4% for 2027-28, rising to 5% in the subsequent fiscal.

CBG sales stood at 115.9 million standard cubic metres (MMSCM) during the April-September period, against combined CNG and D-PNG sales of 6,800 MMSCM. With the combined consumption of the two fuels projected at 13,600 MMSCM for the full fiscal, CBG sales will have to rise to 408 MMSCM to achieve the 3% blending target, requiring an additional 292.1 MMSCM over the first-half volume.
Flagging infrastructure gaps, PNGRB stressed the need to connect CBG plants to gas pipelines to ensure assured offtake and better utilisation of installed capacity.

Of the 210 functional CBG plants in the country, capacity utilisation averages just 44%. More significantly, 247 of the 308 plants under construction currently have no plans for pipeline connectivity.

“A reliable pipeline connection gives CBG plant a buyer every day of the year. Plants with a pipeline, or one being built, use 65-69% of their designed capacity. Better pipeline access means better gas offtake and overall use of every plant,” it said.

Besides expanding pipeline infrastructure, the regulator called on larger entities to establish their own CBG blending targets, increase procurement from independent producers and invest in setting up captive CBG plants.

articles.title: ONGC Q2 net profit jumps 57% on higher crude, gas realisations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: State-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) reported a 57.3% year-on-year (YoY) surge in standalone net profit to ₹15,489 crore for the quarter ended September, supported by higher realisations from crude oil and natural gas.
The company also declared an interim dividend of ₹8 per equity share.

ONGC’s crude oil realisation rose to $92.33 per barrel from $67.34 a barrel in the year-ago quarter. Gas prices from nominated fields increased to $7 per million British thermal units (MMBTU) from $6.75 per MMBTU.
Realisation from new-well gas, previously identified by Chairman Arun Kumar Singh as a key driver of profitability going ahead, climbed to $10.24 per MMBTU against $8.36 per MMBTU a year earlier.
Revenue for the quarter grew 32.8% YoY to ₹43,875 crore.

However, production remained under pressure. Standalone crude oil output declined 4.2% to 4.437 million metric tonnes (MMT), while natural gas production fell 1.6% to 4.839 billion cubic metres (BCM).

Explaining the production dip, ONGC said, “The year-on-year moderation in quarterly production was primarily attributable to reservoir behaviour complexities in KG-98/2 Asset in Eastern Offshore Basin, coupled with monsoon related operational challenges and associated delays in PRP-8 and PRP-9 (Pipeline replacement projects).”
The company added that onshore gas production was affected by lower customer offtake and disruptions at certain major consumer facilities, which temporarily dampened demand.

articles.title: NPCI says MDR charge has been imposed to save the UPI ecosystem from turning ouroboric
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: National Payments Corporation of India (NCPI) has said in the Supreme Court that “zero Merchant Discount Rate (MDR)” for all Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions was no longer sustainable, as functional costs for the phenomenally expanding digital payment industry in India would burn into the public exchequer.

UPI processed as many as 24.51 billion transactions, cumulatively worth approximately ₹29.82 lakh crore, in the month of August 2026 alone, marking its highest-ever monthly volume. An average of approximately 791 million transactions were processed every single day in that month. In Financial Year 2025-26, UPI processed approximately 241.62 billion transactions worth approximately ₹314 lakh crore, the NPCI said.

“The figures illustrate not merely growth, but growth of a magnitude that places correspondingly greater demands on the security, resilience, and infrastructural capacity of the system,” the NPCI, represented by Additional Solicitor General N. Venkataraman, submitted in Court.
The Corporation was responding to a challenge in Court to the government’s decision to introduce an MDR of 0.4% on Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above ₹2,000.

Person to person (P2P) transactions, which account for 70% of total UPI transaction value, would remain completely free irrespective of amount, the NCPI said. There would be no transaction or platform fee or other charge permissible for individuals for sending or receiving money through UPI, it added.

It said person-to-merchant (P2M) payments up to ₹2,000 would also remain “entirely free of MDR”. “This threshold is calibrated to shield the overwhelming majority of everyday, low-value merchant payments of the kind made by ordinary consumers and small merchants alike,” the NPCI said.
The affidavit assured that the amended MDR framework targeted only higher value commerce without disturbing low-value transactions that drive the mass adoption of UPI.

The MDR charge, which did not exceed 0.4%, would apply to P2M transactions above ₹2000. “Effectively, MDR will apply to only about 4% of merchant transactions, and approximately 96% of all P2M will remain unaffected,” the NPCI said.
The NPCI countered the petitioners’ contention that an amended MDR framework should have been introduced only through a new legislation and not just through a notification in September.

The NCPI argued that MDR was not a tax, cess, fee, duty or any other statutory levy imposed by or under a legislative enactment. It was plainly a ‘charge’ collected to recover the huge costs associated with the functioning of the payment system, and was in turn, distributed entirely amongst the participants in the UPI ecosystem.

“MDR is a charge collected by the system participants to recover the costs incurred in running the payment system, and not an imposition pursuant to any delegation of legislative or fiscal power by Parliament, the Central Government or RBI,” the NPCI submitted.

In a 100-page affidavit, the NPCI said that, as a system provider, it had the liberty to determine the MDR applicable to transactions processed through the payment system operated by it, subject to the regulatory framework of the Reserve Bank of India and the prohibition under Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, which exempts UPI transactions below ₹2000 from any charges.

fullParagraphs: Five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards and army said in separate statements, according to local media on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
It regularly attacks ships it accuses of transiting without its authorisation.
The United States military has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait.

"Last night... a large oil tanker attempting to pass through the illegal passageway south of the Strait of Hormuz suffered a fire after striking a mine and was brought to a halt," the Guards told Fars news agency.
"Another supertanker was halted by a massive fire while exiting the eastern Strait of Hormuz. A tugboat that had approached the supertanker to extinguish the fire also caught fire," the Guards said.
The Iranian army later said three more tankers were hit by naval mines.

"Early this morning, a violating oil tanker — navigating through an unsafe area east of the Strait of Hormuz — caught fire and came to a halt after striking a naval mine," the army said, according to the official IRNA news agency.
"Today at around noon, two more oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the unsafe waters east of the Strait of Hormuz," said another army statement carried by IRNA .
There has been no confirmation of the incidents from maritime officials.

British monitor UKMTO reported a tanker being struck by "two unidentified projectiles" around 50 nautical miles (90 kilometres) off the north coast of Qatar, without providing details on any damage or casualties.
That area is around 500 kilometres west of Hormuz, in the centre of the Gulf.

articles.title: Eisenkot tipped to seek Israel government as religious party drops Netanyahu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday (November 5, 2026) as the favourite to be tasked with trying to form an Israeli government as a religious party long aligned with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declined to recommend him.

President Isaac Herzog was holding a second day of consultations with political parties after the October 27 election, in which neither Mr. Netanyahu — a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war — nor Mr. Eisenkot — a former military chief promising to restore national unity — secured enough votes for a majority.
Mr. Herzog will choose for himself whom to ask to form a new government, but traditionally the mandate is given to the person recommended by more parties, which would be Mr. Eisenkot.

The Opposition leader also received a recommendation from a key lawmaker from the Israeli-Arab minority, whose seats in Parliament soared due to outrage over Mr. Netanyahu's policies, even as Mr. Eisenkot has remained unclear on whether he would accept Arab support to form a government.

United Torah Judaism, which backed Mr. Netanyahu after the previous five elections, in its meeting with Mr. Herzog declined to recommend Mr. Netanyahu again as Prime Minister, although it also did not side with Mr. Eisenkot.

The party informed Mr. Herzog "that it has decided not to recommend any member of Knesset to form a government," the President's office said in a statement, referring to the 120-member parliament in which United Torah Judaism has won seven seats.

The party — which represents ultra-Orthodox Jews of Ashkenazi origin, who mostly hail from or have roots in Europe — as well as Shas — which represents the same community but of Sephardic, or mostly West Asian and North African descent — have both been backed by Mr. Netanyahu as they push to maintain the exemption from military service for religious students.

Mr. Netanyahu has preserved the exemption but stopped short of enshrining it in law, in the face of major resentment from many other Israelis as reservists serve multiple tours due to the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.
"In whatever government is next formed, our immediate item is sorting out the status of Torah students," United Torah Judaism lawmaker Isaac Pindrus said.
Mr. Eisenkot, who has tried to appeal to secular Israelis from left to right, has been adamant about closing exemptions from military service.
Some of his Opposition allies have criticised the ultra-Orthodox, who make up about 14% of the population but have far higher birthrates than secular Israelis, as a drain on the State.

Observers say United Torah Judaism's tactic is likely aimed mostly at punishing Mr. Netanyahu and showing that their votes cannot be taken for granted, while they would still serve in a government if he were to form one.

The flight landed safely at the base in Evreux in Normandy, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's office said. All 151 passengers and six crew members are safe and military bomb defusal teams are examining the plane.
Mr. Lecornu's office said that it's following the situation in real time. No other information was immediately released.
Flight tracking sites showed that the Aer Lingus Dublin-Rome flight was approaching Paris when it turned sharply off its trajectory and made several loops before heading toward Evreux.
Several flights across Europe received hoax bomb threats this week that prompted searches, diversions and, in one case, an escort by the Italian air force until landing, officials said.

The flights included Polish airline LOT, Scandinavian Airlines, Wizz Air and Ryanair. The hoax threats came a day after a plane headed for Bulgaria was diverted to Hungary after receiving a similar bomb threat while in the air. No one was injured.

Such threats aren't a new phenomenon but come at a time of increased geopolitical tensions and signs of “disruption,” like attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems, drone incursions in Europe and mysterious triggers to alert apps — even as authorities have warned that hybrid threats abound.

articles.title: ISRO’s latest navigation satellite NVS-03 is fully healthy, says Chairman V. Narayanan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: ISRO’s next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03, launched on October 30 to strengthen India’s NavIC regional satellite navigation system, is “fully healthy”, ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan said on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

Speaking at the inauguration of the statue of legendary astronaut Yuri Gagarin at the Periyar Science and Technology Centre, Mr. Narayanan said, “NVS-03, successfully launched on October 30 midnight, was perfectly placed in the elliptical orbit. From there, we operated the engine of the satellite for 6,400 seconds to the circular orbit. Right now, the satellite is fully healthy. We have to do a lot of in-orbit testing for the satellite payload and others.”

Mr. Narayanan recounted ISRO’s role in ensuring the success of the Axiom-4 mission this summer, which was piloted by Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, the first Indian in space in the last 40 years. Indian scientists had saved the lives of all the astronauts aboard by insisting on scrubbing the initially scheduled launch due to a liquid oxygen leak.

“One day ahead of the scheduled launch on June 11, the countdown had started, and there was a news item about a minor leak. We went ahead with a discussion. I was not satisfied. We insisted on correcting it. Later, we found it was a line crack, not a minor leak,” the ISRO chief explained. “We proved to the world that Indians are second to none, the Indian education system is second to none, Indian training is second to none, to ensure the safety of Gaganyatris [astronauts], including Shubhanshu Shukla,” he added.
The ISRO chief stressed the need to strengthen space technology for better services for citizens. “The work on the fourth launch complex in Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu is under way,” he said.

The ISRO chief recalled Russia’s historic role in boosting India’s space programme. “Then-USSR, and the present Russia has supported us in the space programme a great deal. Using the term MTCR [or Missile Technology Control Regime], nobody was willing to help us. At that point in time, the then-USSR came forward, they were ready to give hardware. USSR was the first country that helped our country send Rakesh Sharma to space and return safely,” said Mr. Narayanan, who spent ten months in Russia in 1993 learning cryogenic technology.

“Today also, we are getting a lot of support. For the Gaganyaan programme also, they are supporting us. We are collaborating in multiple areas. We should not forget the ladder after we have climbed up,” he added.
Russia’s Consul General in Chennai, Valerii Khodzhaev, also said that India and Russia had a “long-lasting relationship.”

articles.title: Postcards from Earth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Somewhere above the plane in which the planets orbit, moving away from the sun at some 17 kilometres a second, a machine older than the internet is closing in on no ordinary milestone. On November 18, Voyager I will be one light-day away from earth.

In 1965, a graduate student in the U.S. named Gary Flandro noticed that around the late 1970s, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune would lie on a single line — something that happens only around every 175 years. So, a spacecraft launched at the right moment could use each planet's gravity to arc towards the next, compressing a 30-year crawl to Neptune into a single decade.
NASA dreamed big at first, but as the budget priorities changed, the plan shrank to two probes aimed only at Jupiter and Saturn. These were the Voyagers.

Scientists and engineers built two nearly identical spacecraft, and launched them 16 days apart: Voyager II first on August 20, 1977, then Voyager I. As it happened, Voyager I would take a faster path that let it overtake its sibling and reach Jupiter first. And from here the two machines lived very different lives.

Voyager I is built like a decagon-shaped drum to pack the electronics and the propellant tank into a light frame. Sixteen thrusters keep a 3.7-metre dish antenna pointing at earth. Three nuclear generators sit at the end of a long boom to keep their radioactivity from corrupting the instruments.
The Voyagers couldn't afford a gram of decoration. They're purely functional objects.
Voyager I and Voyager II each carry a golden phonograph record bolted to their exteriors.

The idea was that the mission ought to carry some kind of message explaining ourselves and our planet to any interstellar intelligence it may encounter that shared none of our biology, language, or history.

Project manager John Casani handed the problem of designing a message to Carl Sagan, who invited the radio astronomer Frank Drake. Their official budget was $1,500 for six weeks — an absurd sum for a message meant to represent an entire species, and in practice it took most of the following year to compose.

They assembled 116 photographs of human anatomy, cities, farms, a mother nursing a child, the structure of DNA, a 12-minute audio collage of surf, thunder, birdsong, humpback whales, and a baby's first cry; greetings in more than 50 languages; and 90 minutes of music from Bach to a Navajo night chant to Chuck Berry's 'Johnny B. Goode'.

At Sagan's request, the documentary maker Ann Druyan spent an hour in a lab with electrodes on her scalp, thinking her way through the history of earth. Two days after she and Sagan had privately agreed to marry, she thought of what it felt like to fall in love. That hour of brain activity was encoded onto the record as sound as well.

Whimsical though it sounds, the record's design posed a significant challenge: how do you write instructions for an alien entity with a different alphabet, units or even senses? So its designers picked something universal: physics. The playback speed was set by the oscillation of a hydrogen atom, location marked by a map of pulsars, the cover plated with uranium-238, whose decay lets a finder calculate exactly how long it has been travelling.

articles.title: What do dark circles under a child’s eyes indicate?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: A child may wake up after a full night’s sleep and still have dark circles under the eyes. For some children, this may simply be a family trait. In others, it could be associated with allergies, persistent nasal congestion or skin conditions. Dark circles, also referred to as periorbital hyperpigmentation, are not a condition in themselves. While parents may immediately associate dark circles with inadequate sleep or nutritional deficiencies, their causes can be more varied.

articles.title: Delhi Police registers FIR over alleged circulation of child sexual abuse material on Meta platforms
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Delhi Police’s Special Cell has registered an FIR over the circulation of suspected child sexual abuse material through Meta platforms, including Facebook and Instagram.

The FIR was registered on October 8 under Sections 67 (publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form) and 67B (publishing or transmitting material depicting children in sexually explicit acts or conduct in electronic form) of the Information Technology Act, 2000.

Approximately 10 links were flagged in a complaint alleging the circulation of such material, following which the police initiated an investigation to verify the allegations, said Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) Additional CP Sanjay Bhatia.

“Acting on our directions, Delhi Police has registered an FIR regarding the availability of Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) on platforms operated by @MetaIndia,” NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo said in a post on X.
The Special Cell is investigating the matter, police said.

articles.title: Climate change increased tropical Cyclone Arnab’s damage by 33%: Study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Climate change increased the damage caused by the tropical Cyclone Arnab, which struck eastern India on October 28, by 33%, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in additional direct economic losses compared to a pre-industrial climate baseline, according to a new study.
ALSO WATCH Cyclone Arnab batters east coast: 5 dead in Andhra Pradesh, 17 Odisha districts affected
It added that the storm brought intense rain, peak 1-minute sustained winds of up to 202 kilometres per hour, and severe damage to infrastructure across Andhra Pradesh.
The study was carried out by researchers at the Imperial College London’s Grantham Institute and published on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

For their analysis, researchers used the Imperial College Storm Model (IRIS) to simulate Cyclone Arnab under current conditions (plus 1.3° Celsius above pre-industrial levels) versus a counterfactual climate without human-induced warming.
“Climate change increased Cyclone Arnab’s maximum wind speed by approximately 5%, and intensified its eyewall rainfall rate by 11% at landfall,” according to the study.

It also revealed that direct damage to physical assets in India was estimated to be 33% higher than it would have been in a pre-industrial climate baseline, attributing roughly 25% of the total economic damage directly to climate change.
ALSO WATCH Beyond Cyclone Arnab: can India tackle the growing cost of natural disasters? | Insight India

In a statement, Dr. Nathan Sparks, researcher at the Department of Physics, Imperial College London, said: “These findings are a powerful reminder of the price of inaction. The costs of climate change are not hypothetical future projections — they are hitting coastal communities in eastern India today.”

articles.title: Helping hand: On Cyclones Arnab and Murasu
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Long-term preparedness and a swift response by authorities minimised casualties when the back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu hit two places of the Andhra Pradesh coast. In Andhra Pradesh, damage from Cyclone Arnab , which made landfall on October 28 was estimated at roughly ₹4,526 crore. Initial estimates of the damage by Cyclone Murasu, which crossed the coast on November 3, indicate that about 52,500 hectares of standing crops were affected. The State reported 12 deaths from the two cyclones. The first cyclone damaged nearly 90,000 hectares of standing crops in southern parts of Odisha. After preliminary on-the-spot assessment of flood-hit areas, the Union government is expected to soon release the first instalment of funds to the affected States. Personnel from Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu have also gone to the rescue of Andhra Pradesh.

The deployment of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) and other technologies has significantly reduced human casualties and property damage. During Cyclone Hudhud in October 2014, Andhra Pradesh reported 63 deaths and damage estimated at nearly ₹22,000 crore. As natural disasters become more frequent in India, greater collaboration is needed between higher learning institutions, especially in science and technology, and central and State government agencies. Authorities must develop an effective compensation framework for saving crops/crop losses. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, a crop insurance scheme that was launched by the Union government a decade ago, has not provided farmers with comprehensive safety cover, as they suffer due to the vagaries of nature. The Union government should improve the scheme so that all farmers are encouraged to bring their crops under the scheme, while State governments should raise awareness about the insurance scheme and support agriculturists by topping up benefits that are under the insurance cover. The Centre should also focus on financial assistance for permanent restoration projects. The initial stand of the Union government was that the National and State Disaster Response Funds were meant for response and relief, not recovery and reconstruction, but following the 15th Finance Commission’s nudge, it added recovery and reconstruction as a component of the two funds two years ago. However, when public infrastructure suffers extensive damage, the Centre should provide additional assistance to ease the burden on affected States. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his team at the Centre must act in the spirit of “cooperative federalism”.
