articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

articles.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself . Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack.

So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. If the fear is that cryptocurrencies are not backed by any asset, then Indian policymakers can choose to allow only stablecoins, which do have real assets underpinning them. Indians are not at higher risk from cryptos than they are from fake stock market scams. The best defence is awareness. By refusing to regulate the crypto space in India and, indeed, taxing it at a prohibitive rate, the government is driving Indians towards either the black market, where such scams proliferate, or foreign exchanges. The government can take a leaf out of Binance’s book and mandate an industry-maintained emergency fund. There is ample international legislation to emulate now. The point is, crypto risks have fallen and adoption is rising. Now is the time to regulate the industry.

articles.title: Business, unusual: On engaging with the Myanmar junta
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Months after a sham election that installed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as Myanmar’s civilian President, the military continues to wage war on its own people even as the world has largely looked away. More than a lakh people are estimated to have died since the 2021 coup, many in fighting between the junta and the anti-coup People’s Defence Forces and ethnic armed organisations. The junta has also killed thousands of civilians in air strikes on villages in rebel-held areas to terrorise communities into giving up their resistance. With wars affecting Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan and Yemen, and Iran, the world has grown numb to such violence. The junta has exploited that indifference and a shifting geopolitical situation to act with impunity. Russia and China, its principal arms suppliers, have stood by it with the former supplying jets that were used to bomb civilians. Beijing, which tacitly allowed three ethnic armed organisations to launch an offensive in Shan and Rakhine States in late 2023, has since pressured two of them into ceasefires and returning seized territory. It also backed the January election. Since being sworn in, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India , Thailand, Vietnam and three other ASEAN member-states. ASEAN still swears by its Five-Point Consensus, which calls for an end to violence and dialogue. Yet, its members seem more than eager to do business with a regime that has flouted every point. Meanwhile, U.S. officials reportedly held secret talks with the junta in Tokyo in June and October, and a senior delegation met Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw in September. Japan is reportedly pressing the Financial Action Task Force to take Myanmar off its blacklist.

The motives are not hard to understand. China wants an outlet to the Indian Ocean and security for its oil and gas pipelines. It has also played both sides, dealing with the junta and powerful rebel groups such as the Kachin Independence Organisation, whose territory is rich in rare earths and jade, and the United Wa State Army, which runs a massive tin mine. New Delhi wants to revive its stalled Act East policy, including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project. The U.S. eyes access to mining vital heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium, for use in electric vehicles and weapons systems. What these short-sighted overtures miss is that trade thrives in a country at peace, not one where armed groups are perennially battling for control. The junta which has killed its citizens and has scuttled every move towards democracy cannot deliver that peace. Unless the generals are made to answer for their war crimes, Myanmar will remain a war zone. It will be ruinous not only for its hapless people but also for businesses seeking to trade with it.

articles.title: United stand: On protests against SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The gathering of hundreds of thousands of people at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, organised by the Congress-led INDIA bloc parties, was a milestone in the battle for the restoration of the integrity of India’s election process. As more and more skeletons tumble out the of the closet of the Election Commission of India (ECI), its chief Gyanesh Kumar has chosen silence while the ruling BJP has rushed to shield him from criticism. The united outcry of protest by the Opposition, led by the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi , is a strong signal of public opinion for the ruling party and India’s institutions, including the ECI, that appear complicit in a scheme that threatens the foundations of Indian democracy. What remains unexplained by the ECI and Mr. Kumar are malpractices in the Special Intensive Revision that could have the effect of subverting the popular will. Protestors on Sunday had arrived from all parts of India, and included people directly affected by the SIR across the country.

The protest reinforced Mr. Gandhi’s central role as the key challenger of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Gandhi, for all his faults, has been an uncompromising champion of constitutional values and pluralism in India. The BJP caricatured him, and even non-BJP voices had bought into the idea of Mr. Gandhi being a privileged dynast out of touch with the commoner. While his ancestry is a matter of fact, so is his tenacity. All Opposition parties mobilised for the protest, but the centrality of the Congress party was unmistakable. Mr. Gandhi has a special focus on subaltern classes to be included in positions of responsibility in the party. The Sunday protest was clearly the largest show of strength in recent memory. The manner in which the Congress coordinated with the wide spectrum of the Opposition, often involving rivals in States, also indicates a clear sense of purpose and pragmatism. The call for the restoration of institutional integrity is the need of the hour; but Mr. Gandhi must be careful not to misstate the nature of the crisis. In his well-reasoned call for accountability of the ECI, Mr. Gandhi ended up questioning the legitimacy of the previous election without providing any substantive basis for his allegations. He must remember that his emergence as the voice of the Opposition places on him the responsibility of being measured in his speeches and his steps.

articles.title: Cascading effect: On dams and land rights
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh.

The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijing has declined to share the former. SUMP thus faces many uncertainties at the outset. Despite India repeatedly raising the issue with China at the highest levels, headway has been limited to Beijing agreeing to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies. Planners have contemplated maintaining the SUMP reservoir at 70% to accommodate unexpected surges, but the level of protection possible if China supplies no advance warning remains unclear. This uncertainty is a thorn in the side of the government’s push against more legitimate resistance by Adi community members and civil rights groups. The need for the project does not excuse the state from following all the relevant laws and protections. The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

articles.title: Kedartal avalancheKedartal avalancheche claims lives of two sisters from Lucknow who shared passion for trekking
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A family’s desperate search for two missing daughters ended in heartbreaking tragedy on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) after the bodies of sisters Vartika Verma and Deepika Verma, residents of Lucknow, were recovered following an avalanche on the Kedartal trekking route in Uttarakhand.

The sisters were among the eight trekkers stranded near Kacchi Dhang, on their way to Kedartal. The group of 13 had set out from Gangotri on October 27, but heavy snowfall and avalanches cut off their route, leaving them stranded in the mountains.

The 26-km trek from Gangotri to Kedartal passes through Kedar Kharak and involves narrow, rocky stretches at high altitude. The glacial lake is situated at about 4,700 metres above sea level, surrounded by high mountain peaks.
With the recovery of two more bodies, the death toll in the avalanche has reached four. Rescue teams are continuing their search for the remaining four trekkers, all friends from West Bengal.

‘Please don’t scroll. Please share’ were the words Atul Verma posted on Instagram, alongside an AI-generated photograph of his younger sisters smiling in the front row of a trekking group. He was desperately trying to draw attention to the missing trekkers and reach someone who could help.

“This is not just a photograph of a trekking group. These are eight human lives, eight families waiting for their loved ones to return,” Mr. Atul Verma wrote in his appeal. He urged people to tag authorities, rescue teams and journalists, and asked them to pray for his sisters and the other trekkers. “One share could help this appeal reach someone who can make a difference,” he said.
The family said they had learnt about the incident through social media and not from the trekking agency.

Mr. Atul Verma then rushed to Uttarkashi, hoping there was still a chance of finding his sisters safe. He reached the district headquarters on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) with other relatives, but was eventually informed that both sisters had died.

The Verma sisters shared a love for trekking and had explored several trails across India and Nepal. Vartika Verma, the younger sister, was a freelance influencer, while Deepika Verma worked as a graphic designer with a private firm. Both had considerable trekking experience. Just two months ago, they had returned from a trip to the Valley of Flowers and Hemkund Sahib in Uttarakhand.
“They were well-equipped and experienced,” Mr. Atul Verma said. The family had never imagined that something both sisters loved so much would end in this way.

The family’s appeal has also questioned the arrangements made by the trekking agency. Their appeal asked if weather advisories had been checked, and if the risks of the high-altitude trek were properly assessed by the trekking agency. Mr. Atul Verma also questioned whether adequate emergency arrangements and guide support had been provided. He called for an investigation into the agency’s role and demanded accountability.”
Teams from the State Disaster Response Force and the Nehru Institute of Mountaineering had recovered four bodies till the noon on Wednesday. The search for the remaining missing trekkers continues.

articles.title: Shifting Jamboo Savari to Rathothsava day was only a suggestion, clarifies Pramoda Devi Wadiyar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Clarifying that her proposal to reschedule the Jamboo Savari from Vijayadashami to Rathothsava day was merely a suggestion, Pramoda Devi Wadiyar of the erstwhile royal family of Mysuru stated that the final decision rests entirely with the State government.

Addressing a press conference on the Mysuru palace premises on Wednesday, Ms. Wadiyar explained that her proposal was aimed at garnering public support rather than offending the government. She noted that the idea was shared via a press statement rather than an official letter to the State government.

Ms. Wadiyar also thanked Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar for assuring her that the government would examine the suggestion and address recent administrative lapses through dialogue, adding that she looks forward to meeting him soon.

Though she said she did not blame the State government for the lapses, Ms. Wadiyar clarified that her grievances were specifically directed at the lack of inter-departmental co-ordination and the “high-handedness of police personnel” at the Brahmapuri and Karikal Thotthi gates of Mysuru palace.

She stated that these lapses disrupted the erstwhile royal family’s traditional religious rituals on Ayudha Pooja and Vijayadashami, prompting her to suggest moving the Jamboo Savari to Rathothsava day.

Addressing the cancellation of this year’s Vajramushti Kalaga (popularly known as Jatti Kalaga ) after the police allegedly denied entry to some wrestlers at the palace gates, Ms. Wadiyar noted that while the centuries-old martial art is a customary palace tradition, it is not a religious ritual.

She pointed out that the event had been cancelled on a few previous occasions as well. Waiting for the delayed wrestlers this year would have caused the family to miss the auspicious muhurtha (scheduled time) for the Vijaya Yatre , part of their private Vijayadashami procession, leaving them no choice but to call off the wrestling bouts.

Responding to reporters’ queries, Ms. Wadiyar asserted that both the Golden Throne and the Ambari (golden howdah) remain the private property of the erstwhile royal family. She explained that the Mysore Palace (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1998, applies strictly to the Mysuru palace and does not extend to other assets listed in the private inventory of the former Maharaja of Mysore. Furthermore, she noted that the 1998 Act itself is currently under legal challenge in court.

Drawing a parallel to the Bangalore Palace dispute, Ms. Wadiyar remarked that although the Karnataka government had enacted the similar Bangalore Palace (Acquisition and Transfer) Act in 1996, the erstwhile royal family continues to retain possession of the palace and its surrounding land while their appeal remains pending before the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Ahead of Amit Shah’s visit, Haryana Congress flags concerns over democracy, law and order
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ahead of the Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s visit to Haryana to lead the Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) ‘Save democracy, remove anarchy’ march, the Haryana Congress on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) put out a series of pointed questions to the ruling party on issues related to democracy, electoral fairness, the independence of constitutional institutions, and the steadily deteriorating state of governance in the State.

“It was astonishing that the BJP, which had failed to provide satisfactory answers to serious questions concerning electoral transparency, was now launching a campaign in the name of saving democracy,” the Congress’s Haryana in-charge Sanjay Dutt said.

“Democracy is not safeguarded merely through slogans, processions and political events. It is protected through transparency, accountability, institutional independence and respect for the people’s mandate. Amit Shah must answer the questions raised by Rahul Gandhi on alleged ‘vote chori ’ [theft] in Haryana in the 2024 Haryana Assembly elections,” a joint statement by Haryana Congress president Rao Narender Singh and Mr. Dutt said.

“Why has the BJP leadership to date failed to provide any concrete and satisfactory response to the specific allegations raised by Mr. Gandhi? Why has no fair, independent and transparent investigation been conducted into the alleged electoral irregularities?” Mr. Dutt added.

“Mr. Shah should also provide answers on who is accountable for the deteriorating law and order situation in Haryana. When the BJP talks about eliminating anarchy, the people of Haryana have every right to ask what concrete steps the State government has taken to ensure their safety. Crimes against women, crimes against children, murders, kidnappings, extortion, gang wars and the growing sense of insecurity among ordinary citizens are matters of serious concern and demand immediate attention,” Mr. Dutt said.

“On November 5, when Mr. Shah leads the BJP’s march in Karnal and addresses a public rally in Ambala, the people of Haryana will expect answers to these important questions,” the Congress leader said.

articles.title: Karnataka HC sentences man to three months’ imprisonment for forging court order
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The High Court of Karnataka has sentenced a man to three months’ simple imprisonment for criminal contempt after he was found guilty of forging a 2017 court order by changing the date and adding the names of some individuals as petitioners who had not filed any petition.

A Division Bench comprising Justices D.K. Singh and H. Shanthi Bhushan passed the order in a criminal contempt of court petition initiated suo motu by the court against Chethan Kumar, a resident of Siddlaghatta in Chickballapur district.

As many as 26 students, who had failed to complete engineering courses within stipulated period, had filed writ petitions before the Vacation Bench, which had passed an interim order on September 28, 2017, directing respondent engineering colleges and the Visveswaraya Technological University to receive their applications for allowing them to appear for exams in backlog subjects.

Later, an advocate for the petitioner-students filed a complaint before the court alleging that the interim order had been fabricated by altering the date from “28.09.2017 to 28.10.2017”, a Saturday when the court was closed, and by adding the names of students who were not petitioners in the original writ petitions.

While the police conducted an investigation and filed charge sheet against Chethan Kumar, the court initiated a separate proceedings under the provisions of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 against him.
During the trial of contempt proceedings, the Bench noted that Chethan Kumar did not deny forging the date of the interim order or adding the names.

Hence, the Bench observed that Chethan Kumar had “attempted to interfere with due course of judicial proceedings and polluted the stream of justice by forging an order passed by this court,” while convicting him.

articles.title: Climate risks pose mounting threats to marine ecosystems, say experts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Marine scientists have warned that warming seas, marine heatwaves, shifting fish populations, coral bleaching, algal blooms and increasingly unpredictable ocean conditions are posing mounting challenges to fisheries and coastal livelihoods.

They expressed these concerns while speaking at the symposium on Societal Applications in Fisheries and Aquaculture using Remote Sensing Imagery, hosted by the Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) here. They suggested integrating diverse expertise to monitor rapidly changing ocean conditions, according to a release.

Around 300 participants from 30 countries, including fisheries scientists, climate and remote sensing experts, and oceanographers, are attending the programme. Marine scientists underscored the growing need to integrate satellite remote sensing, oceanographic observations, climate models, artificial intelligence and in-situ data to better understand the physical and biological changes in marine ecosystems and provide timely advisories and early warnings, the release said.

articles.title: TDP sweeps four Municipal Corporations in A.P. local polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telugu Desam Party (TDP) candidate Manne Srinivasa Prasad (J.B. Srinivas) won the Tirupati Municipal Corporation (TMC) Mayor seat with a majority of 61,582 votes over YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) candidate Y. Vasudeva by the end of counting at S.V. Arts College in Tirupati on Tuesday.

Of the total 1.36 lakh votes polled, Mr. Srinivas received 94,937 votes and Mr. Vasudeva 33,355. While 3,176 votes were achieved by other candidates together, 3,149 votes were considered as invalid and 1,389 votes came under none of the above (NOTA).

Among the 66 wards within the TMC limits, TDP candidates emerged victorious in 38 and YSRCP was successful in 19. The candidates of the Jana Sena Party (JSP), Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and others won three wards each.
Returning Officer and RDO A. Murali presenting the election victory certificate to Matli Suvarna, who won the Kadapa Mayor seat, in Kadapa on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT

In Kadapa, TDP’s Mayoral candidate Matli Suvarna emerged victorious with 1,31,615 votes, gaining a majority of 65,588 votes against YSRCP’s Bandi Deepthi, who received 41,020 votes by the final round of counting at Maulana Azad National Urdu University (MANUU) Polytechnic College.

Of the total 66 wards in the Kadapa Municipal Corporation limits, TDP candidates emerged successful in 61, while JSP and BJP candidates won one and two wards respectively. YSRCP, meanwhile, won one ward. Independent candidates and those of other political parties failed across all wards.

In Nellore, TDP’s Mayoral candidate Poluboina Roop Kumar Yadav defeated YSRCP counterpart Anam Vijaya Kumar Reddy with a huge majority of 80,721 votes after the final round of counting at DKW College in Nellore.

Among the 72 wards in the Nellore Municipal Corporation, TDP candidates were victorious in 56, including 18 unanimously elected wards. JSP and BJP candidates won eight and five wards respectively. Even independent candidates claimed two wards, but the YSRCP won just one.

Prakasam District Election Officer and Collector P. Raja Babu presenting election victory certificate to TDP Mayoral candidate Nallamalli Sri Silpa, after she won the Municipal Corporation elections in Ongole on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: KOMMURI SRINIVAS

In Ongole, TDP Mayoral candidate Nallamalli Sri Silpa beat YSRCP candiate Kuppam Prasad with a huge majority of 37,626 votes. Of the total 62 wards in Ongole Municipal Corporation, TDP candidates were elected in 39, YSRCP in 11, JSP in eight and BJP in one respectively.

articles.title: Centre earmarks ₹2,814 crore to boost lithium, nickel processing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a ₹2,814-crore capital expenditure support scheme to establish domestic processing facilities for lithium and nickel, seeking to strengthen India’s critical mineral ecosystem and reduce import dependence. The scheme will remain in force for five years.

India’s domestic beneficiation and processing infrastructure for critical minerals remains limited, with commercial-scale operations constrained by high capital requirements, limited access to suitable technologies and inadequate availability of raw materials, the government said in a statement.
Union Minister for Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy said the scheme would strengthen domestic capabilities, boost manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports.

“It will benefit key sectors such as electronics, semiconductors, batteries, defence, heavy equipment and machinery, while supporting industries across the manufacturing value chain that utilise critical minerals,” he said in a social media post.
Under the scheme, the government will provide a capital subsidy of 30% of the investment required to establish four critical mineral processing plants — two each for lithium and nickel.
The minimum processing capacity will be 30,000 tonnes (30 kt) each for lithium and 50,000 tonnes (50 kt) each for nickel.
The subsidy will be capped at ₹500 crore per beneficiary for lithium projects and ₹900 crore per beneficiary for nickel facilities.

The four beneficiaries will be selected through a least-cost bidding process, with preference given to technically qualified applicants seeking the lowest capital expenditure support. Incentives will be disbursed in three tranches.

Industry body the Federation of Indian Mineral Industries (FIMI) welcomed the initiative, saying it could encourage fresh investments, increase domestic value addition and strengthen supply chains for battery manufacturing and other strategic industries.
However, it said that securing adequate raw materials would be critical to the scheme’s success.
“Ensuring a reliable supply of raw material through domestic mining and overseas sourcing will be equally important for the success of these processing facilities,” the industry body told The Hindu.
It also underlined the need to develop the entire value chain, from mining to processing and refining, to strengthen India’s long-term mineral security.

articles.title: Union Cabinet approves new VISTAR scheme to overhaul India’s statistical system
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a ₹4,371 crore scheme to overhaul the statistical architecture of the country at both the Central as well as State level, called the Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR) scheme, for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31.

“Aligned with the central objective of Viksit Bharat 2047, the VISTAR Scheme is designed to establish a dynamic, real-time and future-ready official statistical architecture for enhanced timeliness, data granularity, interoperability with harmonised and AI ready datasets,” the government said in a release.

As per the government, the VISTAR scheme will be divided into three components: Comprehensive statistical operations and strengthening of the ecosystem, Support for statistical strengthening, and an Economic Census.

Under the Comprehensive Statistical Operations and Strengthening of Ecosystem component, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has proposed to conduct 59 surveys during the 16th Finance Commission cycle, as compared to 43 major surveys conducted previously.
This, the government said, could potentially fill “critical data gaps in various sectors” and thereby improve decision-making and enable timely and targeted policy interventions.

“In addition, building on recent digital transformations in technology enabled data collection and user-centric dissemination, MoSPI will focus on the end-to-end digitalisation of statistical processes and embedding Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning into regular workflows, primarily for data processing, validation, and analysis,” the government added.

Further, it added that, by mainstreaming alternate sources such as mobile phones, scanners, and e-commerce data, MoSPI will aim to complement traditional surveys, reduce respondent burden, fill data gaps, and strengthen evidence-based policymaking.

Under the support for statistical strengthening (SSS) component, the Centre will provide funds to State governments to help transform the statistical capabilities of States and Union Territories through a redesigned, deliverable-linked framework.

“The vision focuses on building state-level capacity to generate high-quality, granular data at the district and other disaggregated levels, developing indigenous data processing capabilities, and embedding data use cases into localized policymaking,” the government said.

MoSPI will also undertake the 8th Economic Census (EC) in collaboration with the States and Union Territories in order to obtain granular data and activity details of all the non-farm establishments and workers hired down to the gram panchayat and ward levels

This, the government said, would provide an assessment of the unorganised sector of the economy and will serve as the baseline for developing the National Statistical Business Register (SBR) to facilitate targeted enterprise surveys and strategic interventions.

“The economic census data will be extremely useful for planners and policy makers at national and sub-national levels, which will pave the way for estimating the contribution of the unorganised sector to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP),” the government said.

articles.title: Union Cabinet approves ₹14,500 crore VGF scheme to develop large scale energy storage in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Union Cabinet has approved a ₹14,500 crore Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme for the development of grid-scale energy storage systems for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31, the government announced on Wednesday.
According to the government, the scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh of fresh, yet-to-be-commissioned, energy storage capacity across the country.

“The scheme will support creation of new capacities equivalent to 170% of the present-day grid scale energy storage system capacity in the country and help meet the required grid scale ESS capacity of 411 GWh by 2031-32,” the government said in a release.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Can battery storage save India’s renewable energy grid? | Business Matters

The scheme is designed to provide for the development of 60 GWh of hydro pumped storage plant (PSP) capacity, 30 GWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity and 2 GWh of capacity through alternative energy storage technologies, with a total estimated investment of ₹97,600 crore.

“The VGF support will help improve the financial viability of these projects and accelerate the deployment of large-scale energy storage infrastructure in the country,” the government said, adding that the scheme will also provide an impetus to domestic manufacturing of battery energy storage systems.

As per the government’s release, energy storage capacity will be allocated through a tariff-based competitive bidding process with both public and private sector electricity distribution companies eligible for VGF support for BESS and hydro PSP projects.
Projects based on alternative energy storage technologies, too, will be implemented by public and private sector entities.

“To promote indigenous manufacturing, BESS projects will be subject to a minimum Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) of 40%,” the government added. “The requirement will encourage domestic manufacturing, create opportunities for Indian industry and complement existing supply-side incentives for battery manufacturing.”

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The results of the U.S. midterm elections, which show that the Democrats have gained control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, will likely speed up talks between India and the U.S. on a trade deal but could also see higher tariffs on India until the deal is closed, according to experts.

On the one hand, a desire to now quickly close the trade deal to show strength domestically could induce Mr. Trump to increase his tariff pressure on India, while on the other, Indian negotiators will likely see this election result as an opportunity to push through a favourable deal for India.
U.S. midterm elections: Follow LIVE updates from the results on November 4, 2026

According to Ajay Srivastava, founder of the trade think-tank Global Trade Research Initiative, this loss will push U.S. President Donald Trump to increase his exercise of his executive powers to pressure India into accepting a deal.
“With foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win,” Mr. Srivastava said. “Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout.”

Leaders in the U.S. and India have repeatedly said over the last few months that the deal between the two countries is nearly ready and is awaiting final approvals. India, in particular, has been holding out until it receives an assurance that it will win a clear advantage over its competitors.

“Trump will now use his executive powers to pressure India for a quick deal that secures market access for U.S. agricultural and industrial goods, alongside other major concessions for U.S. companies,” Mr. Srivastava said.

While the U.S. Supreme Court in February defanged Mr. Trump’s reciprocal tariff policy that had seen tariffs of up to 50% being levied on India, the President has other tools through which he can levy tariffs.

According to Deep Pal, Director of Geopolitics and Policy at the Koan Advisory Group, the implications of these election results might lead to some difficulty for Mr. Trump in gaining support for his policies.

“For this administration, especially after tonight, any decision has to look like a win domestically, to core Republican voters,” Mr. Pal said. “With Congress out of his hands, a lot will depend on how much control Mr. Trump has over the Republican party and if there will be any purchase for his ideas.”
However, Mr. Pal pointed out that the Indian government might view this new reality in the U.S. with greater optimism.

“Indian negotiators, on the other hand, may think that the new realities will make the Trump administration amenable to a better trade deal for India, breaking the current deadlock, and leading to a flurry of new conversations,” Mr. Pal said.

articles.title: Supreme Court upholds States’ power to levy additional sales tax, says case has become academic
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) held that a 1974 Constitution Bench ruling upholding States’ power to impose additional sales tax or surcharge calculated as a percentage of the existing sales tax continues to hold the field, saying a reference on the issue had become academic.

A seven-judge Constitution Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant unanimously held that the legal question referred to it nearly 27 years ago no longer required adjudication, as the statutory provisions under challenge had since been replaced or amended and the Goods and Services Tax (GST) law had come into force.

“The question referred to is of no practical significance and now academic. Consequently, the question referred to does not survive for adjudication by a seven-judge Bench, and the reference has to be answered accordingly,” the CJI, who wrote the judgment on behalf of himself and five other judges, said.
The Bench also comprised Justices K.V. Viswanathan, S.V.N. Bhatti, Joymalya Bagchi, N.V. Anjaria, Arun Palli and V. Mohana.
Justice Viswanathan wrote a separate concurring verdict.

While declining to undertake a fresh adjudication on the reference, the Court clarified that the five-judge Constitution Bench ruling in S. Kodar vs State of Kerala (1974) continued to hold the field.
The earlier judgment had upheld additional sales tax, rejecting the argument that such a levy amounted to a tax on the income of dealers.

“We have clarified that the case clearly held that an additional tax or surcharge computed as a percentage of the sales tax payable is an enhancement of the rate of sales tax and a tax on the sale or purchase of goods within Entry 54 of List II, as it then stood. That decision continues to hold the field,” the CJI said.
The Court further held that the question of the legislative competence of State legislatures to impose the surcharge would be governed by the law laid down in S. Kodar.

The reference arose from a challenge to Section 5A of the Orissa Sales Tax Act, 1947, which provided for additional tax at the rate of 10% on dealers with an annual turnover between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore, and 15% on dealers whose turnover exceeded ₹1 crore.

The appellants questioned whether the State legislature was competent to impose such a levy under Entry 54 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, which empowered States to tax the sale or purchase of goods, or whether it effectively amounted to a tax on income, a subject falling within Parliament’s domain under Entry 82 of List I.

The controversy stemmed from differing interpretations in earlier Supreme Court decisions. In S. Kodar vs State of Kerala, a five-judge Bench had upheld additional sales tax, ruling that a levy calculated with reference to the sales tax payable was an enhancement of the sales tax rate and not a tax on the dealer’s income.

articles.title: Services sector activity hits 4-month high in October as business conditions improve cautiously
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India's services sector activity recorded the strongest pace of expansion in four months in October as demand buoyancy fuelled growth in business activity and new orders amid easing cost pressures, a monthly survey said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Companies were cautiously optimistic about the outlook, and they lifted jobs to the least extent in four months. The latest expansion in international sales was the weakest in almost four years.
The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Services PMI Business Activity Index rose from 55.2 in September to 55.8 in October, indicating the strongest pace of growth for four months.
In the Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) parlance, a print above 50 means expansion, while a score below 50 denotes contraction.

"India's services PMI rose to 55.8 in October, a four-month high, as business conditions improved cautiously. Although overall demand remained fairly strong, new export orders recorded the slowest pace of expansion since February 2023," Pranjul Bhandari, Chief India Economist at HSBC, said.

Survey participants identified new business growth as the main driver behind the rise in output, the survey said, adding that favourable demand conditions, new client wins and successful advertising boosted new order intakes.

On the prices front, there was a substantial decline in cost pressures. "Input and output prices continued to rise, but at a slower pace than in the previous month, signalling some relief from inflation pressures," Bhandari said.
Employment growth also slowed to its weakest pace since June, suggesting that some service sector businesses have sufficient capacity to meet current staffing requirements, she said.
Companies were, however, cautiously optimistic about the outlook, and they lifted jobs to the least extent in four months.
Meanwhile, India's composite PMI increased to 56.2 in October, from 55.9 in September, marking the fastest rise in aggregate output in four months and reflecting healthy business activity.

"New business intakes at the composite level also expanded at a quicker rate, one that was the most pronounced since June. Yet, job creation softened, and businesses were less upbeat towards growth prospects than they were in September," the report said.
Cost pressures receded at manufacturing firms and their services counterparts, dragging down the aggregate rate of inflation to an 11-month low.

articles.title: Israel’s President accepts certified election results in a blow to Netanyahu’s claim of vote fraud
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) accepted the certified results from last week’s Parliamentary elections as legally binding and said he would begin consultations with party representatives on the formation of a new government.

Mr. Herzog's acceptance of the results as valid dealt a blow to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's effort to discredit the vote in which his religious-nationalist bloc lost its majority in the Israeli parliament, or Knesset, while Arab-led parties made historic gains.
Mr. Netanyahu and his supporters have repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims that the Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, possibly with foreign assistance.

The Israeli President is now required to sit down with various party leaders to determine who to name as Prime Minister-designate — a process that could potentially bring Mr. Netanyahu’s opponents to power.

Israel’s election commission said earlier on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that after a thorough investigation of all parties’ claims of fraud, it had found “no evidence of irregularities that compromised the integrity of the election or affected its results.”
Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud party did not respond to a request for comment.

A separate investigation by the Shin Bet intelligence service, which is headed by David Zini, a Netanyahu appointee and loyalist, into allegations of foreign interference in the election is still ongoing.

In a private meeting on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) of the election committee's members, its head, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, read out an intelligence assessment from the Shin Bet saying the agency believed there had been a “widespread phenomenon involving the influx of substantial funds into Israel from foreign states,” including from countries hostile toward Israel.

The Shin Bet provided no evidence to explain its assertion. The Associated Press obtained a transcript of the assessment from a person who attended the meeting. The person requested anonymity to discuss a closed-door meeting.

The committee has previously said that while claims about foreign actors seeking to influence the election are serious and under investigation, it does not believe that any such interference affected the results — even if it had happened.

Mr. Sohlberg reiterated that stance on Wednesday (November 4, 2026). “At this stage, these are merely suspicions, and even if they are substantiated, the scope of their potential impact is limited,” he said during a ceremony to present the certified election results to Mr. Herzog.
He added that it was dangerous to cast doubt on the results and said they are legally binding.

articles.title: U.S. Midterm election Democrats win five governor races as Hinojosa, Bottoms, Haaland make history
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Democrats are on track for big gains in governor races, notching victories in Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Georgia and Wisconsin, according to U.S. media projections, with a number of other races still too early to call as of early Wednesday (November 4, 2026).

Three candidates made history. In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms became the country’s first Black woman elected governor. In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa became the first Latina governor in the state’s history, unseating a well-financed Republican incumbent in a historically conservative state. And in New Mexico, Democrat Deb Haaland became the country’s first female Native American governor.

A total of three dozen governor races were on the ballot in the elections, with President Donald Trump’s unpopularity and the cost of living at the top of voters’ minds, alongside local concerns ranging from water rights and data centres to cancer rates.
If Democrats can manage a net gain of at least two seats, they will lead a majority of states for the first time since 2010.

Ms. Hinojosa, a Texas state representative, defeated Texas Governor Greg Abbott to become the first Democrat to be elected governor since 1990. She also became the first Latina governor in the state’s history.
Ms. Hinojosa emerged as an unexpected competitor to one of the best-known and best-funded Republican governors in the country. Mr. Abbott outspent her nearly 8-1, according to The Texas Tribune.
Democrats initially wrote off the Texas governor’s race and struggled to find a candidate willing to run against Mr. Abbott.

Both parties viewed the gubernatorial race as an early test of voter sentiment in a state that will likely be a key presidential battleground in 2028.

Mr. Jackson, who spent more than $100 million of his own money on the race, generally aligned himself with Mr. Trump’s agenda, while Ms. Bottoms sought to mobilise the diverse Democratic coalition that helped Joe Biden win the state in 2020.

Ms. Bottoms rose to national prominence in 2020 as she guided Georgia’s largest city through protests, civil unrest and the COVID-19 pandemic. Her base is in the Atlanta metro area, whose rapid growth has reshaped Georgia politics.

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed: The progressive’s progress

fullParagraphs: In a country where, for more than a quarter of a century, the word “Muslim” has been used as an accusation in politics, Abdul El-Sayed’s election as the first Muslim member of the U.S. Senate breaks perhaps the thickest of glass ceilings in American public life. Dr. El-Sayed, a physician and epidemiologist, defeated the Republican former Congressman Mike Rogers with 52.5% of the vote, seven percentage points ahead of his rival.

It would be easy to dismiss this victory as merely a byproduct of the “blue wave” in the U.S. midterms, which carried Democratic candidates to wins even in Republican strongholds such as South Carolina, Texas, and Kansas. But that would be a reductive reading. The odds Dr. El-Sayed faced make the win remarkable in its own right.

articles.title: Apollo Foundation’s hospital in Aragonda blends healthcare with education, nutrition and sanitation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: What if improving the health of a village meant doing more than building a hospital, treating patients and performing surgeries? In Aragonda, a village in Andhra Pradesh’s Chittoor district, an initiative that began with a 50-bed rural hospital has evolved into a community development model that links healthcare with education, nutrition, sanitation and preventive health.

Through its Total Health programme, Apollo Foundation is attempting to address the wider social determinants of health, with interventions spanning different stages of people’s lives, from maternal and child healthcare to youth development, women’s economic independence and elderly care.

The programme’s interventions include 1,200 antenatal and postnatal check-ups for new mothers, training in hygiene practices across 2,600 schools and industry-related and sports skills for more than 545 young people. It has also conducted over two lakh yoga sessions, alongside free screening and care for non-communicable diseases (NCDs), while more than 10.8 lakh meals have been served to elderly people through its geriatric nutrition centres.

Prathap C. Reddy, founder chairman of Apollo Hospitals Group, said the initiative reflected his belief that quality and affordable healthcare should reach every Indian, irrespective of where they lived. While the hospital initially brought modern medicine to his village, the larger vision was to create conditions in which people could lead healthier lives, he said. “Medicine can save lives, but to change the health of a generation, we must also change the conditions in which life is lived,” he added.

Alongside preventive and community healthcare, Apollo Hospitals Aragonda has also expanded its specialised surgical services, completing 1,000 total knee replacement (TKR) procedures. Established as a 50-bed hospital in 2000, it has served more than 1.67 lakh patients and performed over 12,000 surgeries in 26 years.

The knee replacement programme has grown from 100 procedures in 2019 to 500 in 2022 and 1,000 in 2026. “The 1,000 procedures have been completed without a single reported infection,” said Sangita Reddy, joint managing director of Apollo Hospitals.

Telemedicine was another early intervention. With a network of three telephone lines, Apollo connected specialists in cities with patients in rural areas, allowing doctors to examine CT scans and ultrasound images remotely. The initiative enabled specialists to guide local doctors in treating patients who otherwise would have had to travel to distant hospitals. She recalled that former President of US, Bill Clinton, witnessed a telemedicine demonstration from Aragonda during his visit to Hyderabad.

Preetha Reddy, executive vice-chairperson of Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited said the organisation remained committed to narrowing the divide between rural and urban healthcare. “The ability to perform specialised procedures such as knee replacements in a village demonstrates the potential for such models to be replicated in other parts of the world,” she added.

articles.title: The Milky Way grew by devouring galaxies, leaving a trail of ghost stars
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: There have always been stories about them. Australian Aboriginal tales tell of an old couple called the Jukara, while for Chile’s Mapuche people they are Rvganko or water ponds. To modern astronomers, they are the Small and Large Magellanic clouds, two of the closest galaxies to us that are in the process of being swallowed by the Milky Way.

They are evidence of a kind of snowball effect that characterises the formation and evolution of galaxies, which scientists believe are the result of a series of violent collisions. As galaxies fall into one another, the smaller ones are ripped apart by tidal forces of the larger, leaving behind streams and clusters of stars that don’t move in lockstep with the rest of the galaxy. They also stand out for their chemical compositions, which allow astronomers to group stars that were born together and piece back their rough ages.

fullParagraphs: In the summer of 1997, one of the strongest El Niños of the 20th century took shape in the Pacific Ocean. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicted a monsoon rainfall deficit of 8% below the average, as was expected in El Niño years. However, by the end of September that year, rainfall levels were nearly normal.

This year, a “ferocious” El Niño is taking shape, and is expected to peak only in December. The 2026 southwest monsoon ended nearly 13% below the long-term average of 87 cm. East and Northeast India had their driest season since records began in 1901.

articles.title: Why psoriasis can sometimes be hard to diagnose and when you need to see a doctor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Psoriasis is an autoimmune condition that causes thick, scaly patches on the skin. However, it often remains unidentified and undiagnosed because it does not look the same on all parts of the body: it could be mistaken, for instance, for dandruff on the scalp, persistent eczema on the palms, or a fungal infection. You can’t always judge psoriasis by looking only at visible parts of the skin.

Why does this happen? Our skin isn’t the same everywhere. The thickness of the skin can vary considerably depending on the diversity of the environmental conditions that it is exposed to and the kind of treatment given to it. These factors can contribute to how psoriasis appears and feels.

articles.title: Business, unusual: On engaging with the Myanmar junta
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Months after a sham election that installed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as Myanmar’s civilian President, the military continues to wage war on its own people even as the world has largely looked away. More than a lakh people are estimated to have died since the 2021 coup, many in fighting between the junta and the anti-coup People’s Defence Forces and ethnic armed organisations. The junta has also killed thousands of civilians in air strikes on villages in rebel-held areas to terrorise communities into giving up their resistance. With wars affecting Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan and Yemen, and Iran, the world has grown numb to such violence. The junta has exploited that indifference and a shifting geopolitical situation to act with impunity. Russia and China, its principal arms suppliers, have stood by it with the former supplying jets that were used to bomb civilians. Beijing, which tacitly allowed three ethnic armed organisations to launch an offensive in Shan and Rakhine States in late 2023, has since pressured two of them into ceasefires and returning seized territory. It also backed the January election. Since being sworn in, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India , Thailand, Vietnam and three other ASEAN member-states. ASEAN still swears by its Five-Point Consensus, which calls for an end to violence and dialogue. Yet, its members seem more than eager to do business with a regime that has flouted every point. Meanwhile, U.S. officials reportedly held secret talks with the junta in Tokyo in June and October, and a senior delegation met Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw in September. Japan is reportedly pressing the Financial Action Task Force to take Myanmar off its blacklist.

The motives are not hard to understand. China wants an outlet to the Indian Ocean and security for its oil and gas pipelines. It has also played both sides, dealing with the junta and powerful rebel groups such as the Kachin Independence Organisation, whose territory is rich in rare earths and jade, and the United Wa State Army, which runs a massive tin mine. New Delhi wants to revive its stalled Act East policy, including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project. The U.S. eyes access to mining vital heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium, for use in electric vehicles and weapons systems. What these short-sighted overtures miss is that trade thrives in a country at peace, not one where armed groups are perennially battling for control. The junta which has killed its citizens and has scuttled every move towards democracy cannot deliver that peace. Unless the generals are made to answer for their war crimes, Myanmar will remain a war zone. It will be ruinous not only for its hapless people but also for businesses seeking to trade with it.

articles.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself . Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack.

So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. If the fear is that cryptocurrencies are not backed by any asset, then Indian policymakers can choose to allow only stablecoins, which do have real assets underpinning them. Indians are not at higher risk from cryptos than they are from fake stock market scams. The best defence is awareness. By refusing to regulate the crypto space in India and, indeed, taxing it at a prohibitive rate, the government is driving Indians towards either the black market, where such scams proliferate, or foreign exchanges. The government can take a leaf out of Binance’s book and mandate an industry-maintained emergency fund. There is ample international legislation to emulate now. The point is, crypto risks have fallen and adoption is rising. Now is the time to regulate the industry.

articles.title: United stand: On protests against SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The gathering of hundreds of thousands of people at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, organised by the Congress-led INDIA bloc parties, was a milestone in the battle for the restoration of the integrity of India’s election process. As more and more skeletons tumble out the of the closet of the Election Commission of India (ECI), its chief Gyanesh Kumar has chosen silence while the ruling BJP has rushed to shield him from criticism. The united outcry of protest by the Opposition, led by the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi , is a strong signal of public opinion for the ruling party and India’s institutions, including the ECI, that appear complicit in a scheme that threatens the foundations of Indian democracy. What remains unexplained by the ECI and Mr. Kumar are malpractices in the Special Intensive Revision that could have the effect of subverting the popular will. Protestors on Sunday had arrived from all parts of India, and included people directly affected by the SIR across the country.

The protest reinforced Mr. Gandhi’s central role as the key challenger of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Gandhi, for all his faults, has been an uncompromising champion of constitutional values and pluralism in India. The BJP caricatured him, and even non-BJP voices had bought into the idea of Mr. Gandhi being a privileged dynast out of touch with the commoner. While his ancestry is a matter of fact, so is his tenacity. All Opposition parties mobilised for the protest, but the centrality of the Congress party was unmistakable. Mr. Gandhi has a special focus on subaltern classes to be included in positions of responsibility in the party. The Sunday protest was clearly the largest show of strength in recent memory. The manner in which the Congress coordinated with the wide spectrum of the Opposition, often involving rivals in States, also indicates a clear sense of purpose and pragmatism. The call for the restoration of institutional integrity is the need of the hour; but Mr. Gandhi must be careful not to misstate the nature of the crisis. In his well-reasoned call for accountability of the ECI, Mr. Gandhi ended up questioning the legitimacy of the previous election without providing any substantive basis for his allegations. He must remember that his emergence as the voice of the Opposition places on him the responsibility of being measured in his speeches and his steps.

articles.title: Cascading effect: On dams and land rights
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh.

The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijing has declined to share the former. SUMP thus faces many uncertainties at the outset. Despite India repeatedly raising the issue with China at the highest levels, headway has been limited to Beijing agreeing to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies. Planners have contemplated maintaining the SUMP reservoir at 70% to accommodate unexpected surges, but the level of protection possible if China supplies no advance warning remains unclear. This uncertainty is a thorn in the side of the government’s push against more legitimate resistance by Adi community members and civil rights groups. The need for the project does not excuse the state from following all the relevant laws and protections. The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

articles.title: Dwindling support: On the U.S. and the Cuban embargo
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 28, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn.

Amidst these turns, New Delhi must be credited for standing firm on the issue , opposing the embargo, and calling for “dialogue and diplomacy” in its statement. The vote came a month after the BRICS New Delhi declaration expressed “deep concern” over the tightening of unilateral blockade measures on Cuba, and the “worrying humanitarian impact” on the Cuban people. It is important that India continue to stand up to such unilateral measures and amplify the voice of smaller countries, particularly those in the Global South.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.
